title: An ALMA Band 7 survey of SDSS/Herschel quasars in Stripe 82: I. The properties of the 870 micron counterparts
question: Unambiguously identify the submillimeter counterparts of a statistical sample of 152 FIR-bright SDSS quasars in Stripe 82, estimate their real multiplicity rates, and assess the role of mergers in triggering concomitant SMBH accretion and extreme star formation.

what.value: Parent sample of FIR-bright SDSS quasars and FIR-derived star formation rates

evidence.quote: The quasar sample under study is drawn from the parent sample of FIR-bright SDSS quasars in the HerMES (cite: oliver12) fields analysed in (cite: pitchford16).

evidence.loc: On the extreme star formation rates
evidence.quote: More than half the $z>1$ quasars in the parent sample of (cite: pitchford16), and 56% of the quasars in our sample exhibit FIR-derived SFRs exceeding 1000 M$_{\odot}$yr$^{-1}$.

what.value: SDSS DR16 quasar catalogue redshifts and BAL probabilities (BAL_PROB, BI, AI)

evidence.quote: As the parent sample was drawn from more than a decade old SDSS data releases, the quasars in the sample were checked against the SDSS Data Release 16 (DR16) quasar catalogue, that encompasses all of the quasars from previous releases (cite: lyke20).

For the SDSS DR16 quasar catalogue, an automatic procedure was put in place to identify HiBAL quasars based on the values of the Balnicity and Intrinsic Absorption indices (BI and AI, respectively), derived mainly from the CIV emission line, as described in (cite: lyke20).

what.value: 1.1 mm submm number counts in deep ALMA fields SSA22 and GOODS-ALMA

evidence.quote: In order to assess the probability of the secondary submm counterparts found by the present analysis not being chance associations, but, instead physical pairs or triplets, we compared the number counts in the fields of the quasars with those derived from submm number counts at 1.1 mm in deep ALMA fields, namely SSA22 (cite: umehata17) and GOODS-ALMA (cite: franco18).

what.value: 4XMM-DR14 X-ray source catalogue and Chandra Source Catalogue Release 2.1

evidence.loc: CO transitions in the low resolution spectra
evidence.quote: We identified 27 matches in the 4XMM-DR14 catalogue (cite: webb2020) within 5$''$ of the SDSS quasar coordinates.

evidence.loc: CO transitions in the low resolution spectra
evidence.quote: We also identified eight matches in the Chandra Source Catalogue Release 2.1 (cite: evans2024), but none were expected to show CO emission.

recipe.goal: Source identification and continuum photometry on Band 7 maps
recipe.method: Custom-made Python script computing MAD and RMS (within +/-5*MAD), identifying peaks >5 sigma, extracting flux in a box aperture of width 2x beam major axis, computing light-weighted centroid (>3 sigma), fitting with CASA imfit in an elliptical aperture of 2x beam size, and performing forced photometry at phase centre for non-detections
key_parameters: Detection threshold: 5 sigma peak flux; forced photometry threshold: 3 sigma peak flux
Box aperture width = 2x beam major axis; elliptical imfit aperture = 2x beam size

recipe.goal: Multiplicity analysis as a function of 250 um flux, redshift, Eddington ratio, and BAL classification
recipe.method: Count submm counterparts per quasar field, compute fractional contribution of primary, secondary, and tertiary sources to total 870 um flux above and below S_250 = 45 mJy, evaluate multiplicity rates across four redshift bins (1-1.5, 1.5-2, 2-2.5, >2.5) with Poissonian errors, and compare multiplicity incidence in visually confirmed HiBAL quasars vs the full sample
key_parameters: Primary counterpart matching radius < 0.5'' from optical quasar coordinates
250 um flux division at S_250 = 45 mJy

recipe.goal: Targeted and blind search for serendipitous emission lines (CO, H2O, HCN)
recipe.method: Extract 1D spectra for all 209 continuum detections within an aperture matching the synthesised beam size and PA, visually inspect spectra and ALMA pipeline findcont plots for peaks >3 sigma per channel near expected transitions, fit detected lines with a Gaussian, and perform an independent blind search on continuum-subtracted smoothed data cubes using SoFiA
key_parameters: Line reliability threshold: >3 sigma per channel in binned spectrum within SDSS redshift uncertainty of 0.002
SoFiA smoothing kernels: 3, 6, 9 pixels spatially (~0.14'' pixel scale) and 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 channels in velocity (~28 km/s channel width)
assumptions: Typical quasar CO spectral line energy distribution (COSLED) from van der Werf et al. (2010) and Carilli & Walter (2013) to evaluate high-J sensitivity

recipe.goal: Comparison of secondary counterpart number counts with deep ALMA blank fields
recipe.method: Compare the incidence and radial distribution of the 67 secondary counterparts across the total survey area (~9.8 arcmin^2) against scaled 1.1 mm field number counts from SSA22 and GOODS-ALMA
key_parameters: Total survey area = ~9.8 arcmin^2 across 152 fields
assumptions: Modified black body model with dust emissivity beta = 1.5 and dust temperature T = 35 K, yielding S_1.1mm / S_870um = 0.56

score_reason: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration and imaging with exact CASA and pipeline versions stated (6.4.1.12 / 2022.2.0.64), clear step-by-step description of the continuum extraction algorithm, and full catalog published at CDS; minor deductions for unreleased custom Python script and unstated primary-beam handling for off-axis companions.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Cycle 9 dataset (2022.1.00029.S) reduced entirely with the standard ALMA pipeline; the primary numeric results (number of >5 sigma detections, multiplicity fractions vs redshift and 250 um flux, and 5 serendipitous CO line fluxes/FWHMs) can be directly reproduced from the pipeline products.
